transcript.text:
Thank you both for those critical findings. Let me summarize where we stand and what I'm prepared to do.

Daniel, the conflicts issue you've identified is serious. If Atlas currently advises a company whose confidential product roadmap is relevant to our patent case, we cannot proceed without written informed consent from that company, an ethical wall barring the conflicted lawyers from this matter, and a prohibition on using that company's confidential information. I will not approve this engagement — conditionally or finally — until that consent is obtained and documented.

Maya, the procurement picture is equally clear. Our approved benchmark is $350 per hour with a $210,000 matter cap. Atlas's proposed $425 rate and $260,000 budget both exceed those benchmarks. We need to either negotiate Atlas down to those figures or document a justified exception, and I'd strongly prefer negotiation before considering an exception.

Given both of these open items, I'm prepared to record a conditional approval with the following concrete follow-up commitments: (1) Daniel completes his final ethics classification on the conflicts memo and we obtain written informed consent from the affected company before any work begins; (2) an ethical wall and confidentiality prohibition are formalized in the engagement letter; (3) Maya uploads the benchmark confirmation to the procurement intake file and we negotiate Atlas's rate and budget down to our approved benchmarks — or document a justified exception if negotiation fails. Final approval will not issue until all of these are resolved.

Does anyone see any issues with proceeding on that basis?
